report.summary: Chunk 5 of 7 of daedalus/council/bus.py: defines _file_sig, _chain_state, _ends_without_newline, _write_anchor, _chain_records, and append_round. Claims about caching, locking, atomicity, and ordering are checked.
risks: _chain_state | high | Caching relies on file signature; cross-process changes might not invalidate if size unchanged? | Check if mtime_ns changes on cross-process write.

_chain_records | medium | Leading newline insertion for torn tails could produce empty line if prefix is 
 and file ends with 
? | Review logic: _ends_without_newline returns False if file ends with 
, so prefix is '' in that case.
append_round | medium | Refusal receipt may be generated twice if first attempt also triggers rule; anonymous flag used. | Verify _scan_turn behavior on receipt.
append_round | low | Duplicate actor per round not checked; claim says it's a caller bug. | No validation code present.

handoff.purpose: Define internal chain helpers and public append_round function.

symbols.name: _file_sig
symbols.note: Returns (size, mtime_ns) tuple or None if file not found.

symbols.name: _chain_state
symbols.note: Returns dict with sig, tail, count, turns; caches result keyed by resolved path and invalidated on file signature change.

symbols.name: _ends_without_newline
symbols.note: Returns True if file exists and last byte is not newline.

symbols.name: _write_anchor
symbols.note: Writes anchor JSON file to anchor_path(store_path).

symbols.name: _chain_records
symbols.note: Chains a batch of records and appends to store file; returns list of ids. Must be called under _WRITE_LOCK.

symbols.name: append_round
symbols.note: Public API: normalizes, floors, sorts turns, chains them as a round, and appends to store.

claims.text: Tail entry_sha + record/turn counts, cached and invalidated by file signature.
claims.why: Function computes tail, count, turns from records and caches with sig key; invalidates on sig mismatch.
No lock acquisition shown in this chunk; callers must ensure.

claims.text: Any cross-process append changes the size, forcing a reload, so a stale ``prev`` can never be bound.
claims.why: Cache is invalidated if file signature (size, mtime) changes; cross-process append changes size.

claims.text: One chain timestamp for the whole batch: ``ts`` is inside ``entry_sha``, so per-turn wall clock would make the head depend on completion order.
claims.why: ts is computed once and used for all records in the batch; entry_sha includes ts.

claims.text: Read-then-write happens inside the lock so a concurrent append can neither tear a line nor bind two lines to one ``prev``.
claims.why: Lock acquisition not shown; code uses _WRITE_LOCK but no evidence of exclusive access.

claims.text: A torn (newline-less) tail is separated with a leading newline so this batch lands as its own parseable lines instead of fusing onto the fragment and being destroyed while the caller holds a success id.
claims.why: Code checks _ends_without_newline and prepends newline if needed.

claims.text: ``turns`` may arrive in ANY completion order.
claims.why: No sort shown in this chunk; sorting may occur elsewhere or later.

claims.text: Turns are normalised, secret-floored, then sorted by actor id and chained with ``seq`` assigned here -- so reversed completion order yields a byte-identical chain head.
claims.why: Normalization and flooring are called (_normalize_turn, secret_floor_rule implied), but sorting by actor id is not visible in this chunk.

claims.text: Exactly one turn per actor per round is allowed: a duplicate is a caller bug that would double a voice, and a missing participant must be recorded as an ``unavailable`` turn rather than skipped.
claims.why: No duplicate check or validation for missing participants in this chunk.

claims.text: a round with no turns is not a round: every requested participant produces exactly one chained turn
claims.why: Code raises ValueError if turns is empty.

claims.text: REFUSE. The offending bytes never reach the file -- not in the turn, and not in the receipt.
claims.why: If _scan_turn returns a rule, rec is replaced with a receipt; original rec not written.

claims.text: If _scan_turn(receipt) is not None: receipt = _refusal_receipt(rec, rule, anonymous=True)

observations.what: _chain_state caches state keyed by resolved path and invalidates on file signature change.
_ends_without_newline checks last byte of file; used by _chain_records to insert leading newline.
append_round normalizes turns and applies secret floor rule via _scan_turn; if rule triggers, replaces turn with refusal receipt.
append_round does not sort turns by actor id in this chunk; sorting may be done elsewhere or missing.
append_round does not check for duplicate actor ids; relies on caller.
